newsitem.title: INDIA: India cabinet panel to speed infrastructure growth.
newsitem.headline: India cabinet panel to speed infrastructure growth.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda has set up a cabinet panel on infrastructure to speed up implementation of projects and clear bottlenecks in the sector, a government spokesman said on Saturday.

"The committee, besides broadly overseeing the various projects under implementation, will also provide overall policy initiatives, steps to remove bottlenecks and provide a coordination mechanism," he said.
The committee would consist of the Finance Minister, Railways Minister, Junior Petroleum Minister, Surface Transport Minister and the deputy chief of the Plan panel.
Slow growth in key infrastructure sectors in the first five months of the 1996/97 (April-March) fiscal year has fuelled fears of an industrial slowdown.
The six key infrastructure sectors -- coal, steel, crude oil, power, cement and petroleum products -- grew 3.5 percent during April-August compared with 11.7 percent in the same period last year.
The spokesperson quoted Deve Gowda as saying that better performance in infrastructure sectors was the key to faster economic growth.
India expects GDP growth of 6.6 percent in the current fiscal year ending next March 31.
